title: Chess Surgery
summary: Retreat with the king and preserve a pawn tempo so the king can lead its passer.

nodes.question: Which approach lets Black’s king lead its pawn?
nodes.explanation: Black has Kf8 and g7 against Kc1 and h4. The closer black king has a win, but the h-pawn can divert it or force a drawn rook-pawn ending.

branches.title: Retreat and advance the pawn only one square
commentary: Begin with Black to move in the complete four-piece source root. The winning route preserves room in front of the g-pawn.
Kf7 approaches while keeping a retreat to g8 available.
h5 controls g6 and prevents the direct king approach through that square.
Kg8 retreats to approach h6 through h7, keeping g6 free for the pawn.
h6 offers the last white pawn as a distraction.
g6 advances just one square. Black reserves g5 for its king rather than occupying it with the pawn.
Kd2 starts the white king’s march toward the promotion path.
Kh7 approaches h6 from above.
Ke3 continues White’s fastest illustrated central approach.
Kxh6 removes the white pawn and leaves a g-pawn, avoiding the rook-pawn trap.
Kf4 tries to get in front of the remaining pawn.
Kh5 reaches a square ahead of g6. Black retains an exact win; this selected line ends before normal pawn conversion.

branches.title: Approach directly and accept the sacrifice
commentary: Compare the source’s direct approach and rook-pawn warning, with independently supplied representative king moves to show the actual stalemate.
Kf7 approaches the pawns.
h5 bars g6 and prepares the pawn sacrifice.
Kf6 gives up the forced win by allowing White to divert the g-pawn.
h6 offers the pawn to turn g7 into a rook pawn.
gxh6 accepts the offer. With accurate play, White reaches the promotion corner in time.
Kd2 begins an independent representative route toward h1.
Kg5 approaches with the king.
Ke3 continues toward the corner.
Kg4 moves closer but cannot keep White from h1.
Kf2 heads toward g1.
h5 advances the rook pawn.
Kg1 reaches the corner’s entry square.
h4 advances again.
Kh1 occupies the promotion corner.
Kg3 supports the pawn but cannot evict the white king.
Kg1 uses the available neighboring square.
h3 pushes toward promotion.
Kh1 returns to the corner.
h2 is actual stalemate in this representative continuation: g1 is attacked by the pawn, while g2 and h2 are controlled by the king.

branches.title: Spend both pawn tempi at once
commentary: Compare the source’s two-square pawn advance with the winning one-square move.
Kf7 starts the approach.
h5 blocks g6 for the king.
Kg8 sets up the retreating route.
h6 offers the pawn.
g5 gives away the win: the pawn occupies the square its king needs to lead from.
Kd2 starts White’s central march.
Kh7 goes toward the offered pawn.
Ke3 closes the distance.
Kxh6 removes h6, but now Black’s g-pawn is already on g5.
Kf3 approaches the blocking squares.
Kh5 reaches alongside its pawn rather than ahead of it. The exact king-and-pawn ending is drawn with best play.
branches.explanation: Kh5 reaches alongside its pawn rather than ahead of it. The exact king-and-pawn ending is drawn with best play.

exercises.answer: The king needs h5 ahead of a pawn still on g6. After ...g5 the same king route reaches alongside its pawn and White can block it.
